plan.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) at Thanksgiving dinner: does the GLP-1 pill have to be taken on an empty stomach? What the US label says about food and water
plan.angle: Orforglipron (Foundayo) at Thanksgiving: does the pill need an empty stomach? By 6 s, give the PI section 2 wording: take it once daily, with or without food, at any time of day (US PI rev 7/2026). Then, as a separate label sentence: nausea is common, mostly during dose escalation, and decreased over time. Add 2 untagged tips at most: a smaller first plate and eating slowly. Add the low-blood-sugar caveat for diabetes plus insulin or a sulfonylurea. Then the emergency card in Medication Guide wording, the scoped don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line. Don't quote 'without food or water restrictions' as label text.
plan.working_title: Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill at Thanksgiving: Empty Stomach? #shorts
plan.why: Spin-off of L1. It pairs an approved drug name people search for with a holiday practical moment, which is the pattern behind our 826-view Foundayo Short. | fact-check: This is a good practical myth-flip, and the fact behind it holds up: the US PI says Foundayo is taken once daily, with or without food, at any time of day, and it found no clinically relevant food effect. However, 'without food or water restrictions' is Lilly's marketing and medical-information phrasing. Don't put that phrase in quotes or credit it to the PI unless you find it in the PI text itself. Section 2 of the PI is the source to quote. Don't compare it with other pills (e.g. Rybelsus). Only include a nausea rate vs placebo if it matches L1's verified script exactly. Keep 'mostly during dose escalation and decreased over time' as its own sentence. The low-blood-sugar caveat covers diabetes plus insulin or a sulfonylurea. Don't imply zero risk otherwise. Use the full emergency card wording and add the scoped don't-stop line. Leave out dose timing schedules and any suggestion to skip or move a dose for the holiday meal.

package.title: Foundayo (Orforglipron) Pill at Thanksgiving: Empty Stomach? #shorts
package.description:
One Foundayo (orforglipron) pill a day, with or without food, per the US label, even on Thanksgiving. Nausea is common on Foundayo. The label says it was higher while the dose was being stepped up, and decreased over time.
Severe stomach pain that will not go away, with or without vomiting? Call your healthcare provider right away.
For anything that isn't that emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#Orforglipron
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
I checked this Short against the live FOUNDAYO US Prescribing Information (uspl.lilly.com/foundayo, rev. 7/2026). It passes, with two small wording fixes listed below.

What the label supports:
- **s1 and s2:** Section 2.1 says "Take FOUNDAYO orally once daily, with or without food." The empty-stomach correction and the hook are accurate, and the Short delivers what the title promises.
- **s3:** Section 6.1 shows nausea in 26%, 34% and 35% of people on the 5.5 mg, 9 mg and 17.2 mg doses, versus 10% on placebo, so "common" is fair. The label also says "the incidence of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea was higher during the FOUNDAYO dosage escalation period and decreased over time", which matches the narration and the card.
- **s5:** Section 5.5 is Hypoglycemia, as cited. The label warns about use with insulin or an insulin secretagogue, and in Trial 2 (adults with type 2 diabetes) 7% of people also taking a sulfonylurea reported low blood sugar, versus 0.5% of those not taking one. It also states that hypoglycemia "has also been associated with FOUNDAYO and GLP-1 receptor agonists in adults without type 2 diabetes."

Script rules:
- The safety lines, the scoped don't-stop line, the prescriber close and the loop ending all follow the channel rules.
- There's no subscribe line and no "link in the description".
- I count about 157 words, inside the 135–160 standard arm.
- The two tips (s4) are general eating-comfort tips with no source tag and aren't credited to a study.

Two minor fixes:
1. **s5:** The label's wording is "without type 2 diabetes", not "without diabetes".
2. **s6:** The pancreatitis wording conflicts with our own notes. I fetched the label three times. Each time, section 17 and the Medication Guide quoted "…that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting", and section 5.2 says "nausea or vomiting". That contradicts the 11-21 playbook note telling us to drop "nausea". The script's narrower "with or without vomiting" doesn't put anyone at risk, but it isn't verbatim. A person should check the PDF and settle it.

The one source checked out and has a working URL.

issues.claim: The label reports it without diabetes too. / Also reported without diabetes.
issues.problem: Section 5.5 says hypoglycemia has been associated with FOUNDAYO 'in adults without type 2 diabetes.' Saying 'without diabetes' widens the label's scope a little. The playbook asks for 'adults without type 2 diabetes'.
issues.fix: Narration: "The label reports it in adults without type two diabetes too." On-screen text: "Type 2 diabetes + insulin or a sulfonylurea: higher low blood sugar risk. Also reported without type 2 diabetes." List item 4: "Also reported without type 2 diabetes"

issues.claim: Severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away, with or without vomiting: call your healthcare provider right away.
issues.problem: I fetched the live FOUNDAYO label three times. Each time, section 17 and the Medication Guide read '…severe pain in your stomach area (abdomen) that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting', and section 5.2 says 'may or may not be accompanied by nausea or vomiting'. The script's 'with or without vomiting' follows the 11-21 playbook note ('never add nausea'), which appears to have come from the Zepbound/Mounjaro wording. Our wording doesn't put anyone at risk, because 'with or without' still covers pain with nausea. But it isn't the Foundayo Medication Guide's exact wording, and it conflicts with that playbook rule.
issues.fix: Have a person check the Foundayo Medication Guide PDF. If it confirms 'with or without nausea or vomiting', change the narration to: "If you have severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting, call your healthcare provider right away." Change the on-screen text to: "Severe stomach pain that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting? Call your healthcare provider right away." Then update the playbook so the 'no nausea' rule applies only to tirzepatide labels. This adds 2 words, bringing the Short to about 159, still within 160. If the PDF reads 'with or without vomiting', keep the script as it is.
